spans.s:
Pīlā occurs once in the Atharvaveda^1 as the name of an
 Apsaras, being no doubt originally a name of some fragrant
[]
plant, like Naladī and Guggulū, two other names of Apsarases
given in the same verse.
1) iv. 37, 3. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 69; Whitney, Translation of the
Atharvaveda, 211.

Pīlu is the name in the Atharvaveda^1 of a tree (Careya arborea
or Salvadora persica) on the fruit of which doves fed.
1) xx. 135, 12. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 62; Weber, Transactions of
the Berlin Academy, 1895, 861.

Pīlumatī is in the Atharvaveda (xviii. 2, 48) the name of the
intermediate heaven lying between the udanuvatī, ‘watery,’ and
the pra-dyauḥ, ‘farthest heaven.’ It presumably means ‘rich
in Pīlu.’ Cf. Div.
